mcqs.question: A person lifts a 20 kg box vertically through a height of 5 m in 4 s. What is the average power delivered during the lift? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = m g h = 20 kg × 10 m/s² × 5 m = 1000 J. Average power = total work / total time = 1000 J / 4 s = 250 W. Hence option A is correct. The other options result from incorrect division or using distance instead of time.

mcqs.question: A car of mass 1000 kg is moving such that at a particular instant its speed is 20 m/s and the net driving force on it is 4000 N. What is the instantaneous power supplied by the engine at that instant?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P = F·v. Here F = 4000 N and v = 20 m/s, so P = 4000 × 20 = 80 000 W = 80 kW. Option B is correct. Option A would be half the correct value, C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: A 60 W bulb is said to consume 60 J of energy each second. A student thinks that if the bulb is kept on for 2 minutes, it still consumes only 60 J of energy. Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: Energy = Power × time, so the bulb uses 60 W × 120 s = 7200 J.
options.B: Energy = Power ÷ time, so the bulb uses 60 W ÷ 120 s = 0.5 J.
options.C: Power and energy are the same physical quantity, so the bulb always uses 60 J.
options.D: The bulb’s energy consumption does not depend on time.

mcqs.answer: Energy = Power × time, so the bulb uses 60 W × 120 s = 7200 J.
mcqs.explanation: Power is the rate of energy transfer. Energy consumed = Power × time. For 2 minutes (120 s), energy = 60 W × 120 s = 7200 J. Hence option A correct. Options B, C, D misuse the relationship between power and energy.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A constant horizontal force of 10 N pushes an object that moves at a constant speed of 3 m/s. What is the power delivered? If the speed doubles while the force stays the same, how does the power change?

options.A: 30 W initially and it doubles to 60 W when speed doubles.
options.B: 30 W initially and it remains 30 W when speed doubles.
options.C: 10 W initially and it doubles to 20 W when speed doubles.
options.D: 30 W initially and it halves to 15 W when speed doubles.

mcqs.answer: 30 W initially and it doubles to 60 W when speed doubles.
mcqs.explanation: Power P = F·v. Initially P = 10 N × 3 m/s = 30 W. If speed becomes 6 m/s, P = 10 N × 6 m/s = 60 W, i.e., it doubles. Option A captures both values correctly. The other options misapply the formula.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes average power from instantaneous power?

options.A: Average power is total work divided by total time, while instantaneous power is the derivative of work with respect to time at a particular instant.
options.B: Average power equals force times velocity at any instant, while instantaneous power is work divided by total time.
options.C: Both are calculated the same way; there is no difference between them.
options.D: Average power is always larger than instantaneous power.

mcqs.answer: Average power is total work divided by total time, while instantaneous power is the derivative of work with respect to time at a particular instant.
mcqs.explanation: Average power = ΔW/Δt over an interval. Instantaneous power = dW/dt at a specific moment. Option A states this precisely. Options B, C, D are incorrect definitions or false statements.

mcqs.question: A particle moves along a straight line under a force F = 6t² N, where t is in seconds. If the particle’s velocity at t = 2 s is 8 m/s, what is the instantaneous power at that instant?
mcqs.explanation: At t = 2 s, force F = 6×(2)² = 24 N. Instantaneous power P = F·v = 24 N × 8 m/s = 192 W. Option B is correct. Options A, C, D arise from arithmetic errors (e.g., missing factor of 2).

mcqs.question: A machine does 500 J of work in 5 s. What is its power?
mcqs.explanation: Power = Work / time = 500 J / 5 s = 100 W. Option A is correct. The other options result from incorrect division or multiplication.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: Which expression correctly gives the power when a constant force F acts on an object moving with constant speed v?
mcqs.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, and for constant force and velocity, P = F·v. Option B states this correctly. Options A, C, D misuse the relationship.
